method: built-in image_gen; one subject per call; style board attached to every call, surya.png also attached for the two edits

subjects.name: chandra
subjects.prompt: Create ONE production icon asset on a truly transparent RGBA background. Reference role: the supplied image is the approved Storybook miniatures style board — match its style exactly, but paint the NEW subject described below; do not copy any subject from the board. Match the reference matte earthy burnt ochre, muted gold/brass, warm brown outlines, subtle hand-painted shading and delicate grain. Crisp simple shapes must read at 25 logical pixels. Center the visible bounding box exactly in a square canvas; generous equal transparent margins; the subject occupies about 78% of the canvas in its longest dimension. Flat front-facing miniature, no surrounding frame, no tile, no badge, no ground shadow, no scenery, no cast shadow, no checkerboard, no text, letters, numerals, currency signs or labels. Do not change the palette to shiny yellow, vivid orange or glossy 3D. Subject: An ivory crescent moon opening to the right, soft warm-sepia shading on its inner edge and two faint craters, with one small five-pointed muted-gold star in the crescent's opening.

subjects.name: sunset
subjects.prompt: Edit the supplied transparent painted rising-sun icon (surya.png) to create ONE matching icon asset for this same native mobile app; the second supplied image is the approved Storybook miniatures style board for palette and grain. Keep the reference's horizon line, warm brown hand-painted outline weight, matte watercolor grain, frontal composition, canvas size and equal transparent margins essentially identical. Genuine transparent RGBA outside the subject, no tile, scenery beyond the horizon line, cast shadow, glow, glossy metal, checkerboard, text or watermark. Crisp shapes must read at 25 logical pixels. Change ONLY the following: make the sun SETTING — the disc sits lower, more than half below the same horizon line, in a deeper amber-rose pigment, with shorter and fewer rays, and two tiny distant birds in warm brown flying left above the horizon.
